papers.title: Comparisons of benchmark equivalence relations
papers.abstract:
We determine all Borel-reducibility comparisons within the family of benchmark equivalence relations in Gao's monograph, enlarged by the universal treeable relation $E_{\infty T}$ and its countable power $E_{\infty T}^\omega$. We prove $E_\infty^\omega\leq_B c_0$, $E_\infty
leq_B\ell_p$ for $2<p<\infty$, $\ell_p
leq_B{\equiv_m}$ for $2<p<\infty$, $c_0
leq_B{\equiv_m}$, $c_0
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$, and $\equiv_m
leq_B\ell_\infty^+$. Together with the classical result, these give $\ell_p\leq_B{\equiv_m}$ exactly when $p\leq2$. The same methods show that $E_{\infty T}$ is incomparable with every $\ell_p$, $1\leq p<\infty$. The comparisons answer questions recorded in Gao's monograph and Kanovei's monograph. We also prove that unitary equivalence of all bounded linear operators is not Borel reducible to $\equiv_m$, answering a question of Ding and Gao. Equivalently, unitary equivalence of arbitrary representations of $F_\infty$ is strictly more complicated than that of arbitrary representations of $\mathbb Z$, answering a question of Thomas.

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $\phi$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $\phi^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $\phi^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $\phi$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the L\'evy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: Strongly stable fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field which is strongly stable, that is, stable and strongly dependent. Then $K$ is finite or algebraically closed. This answers a question of Shelah.

papers.title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

papers.title: Loose Inductive Set Theories
papers.abstract: We prove that KP, with Full Set Induction, is neither solid nor tight. More generally, every consistent theory obtained from KPC by adding a quantifier bounded set of sentences has a model with a parameter-free definable class surjection from its natural numbers onto its universe. Using such enumerations to define generic extensions by relative interpretations, we show that theories with the stable definable ground property are not tight. Ground definability over MOST and continuum coding over ZFC^{\Pi_3} yield applications to weak inductive set theories with large cardinals and forcing axioms. Finally, solidity for quantifier bounded extensions of MOST with Full Set Induction implies a Ground Axiom formulated using a fixed finite level of genericity; under the same solidity hypothesis, the corresponding extension of full ZFC proves the ordinary Ground Axiom.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
papers.abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game. To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL. The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.

papers.title: Decidability in First-Order Modal Logic with Non-Rigid Constants and Definite Descriptions
papers.abstract: While modal extensions of decidable fragments of first-order logic are usually undecidable, their monodic counterparts, in which formulas in the scope of modal operators have at most one free variable, are typically decidable. This only holds, however, under the provision that non-rigid constants, definite descriptions and non-trivial counting are not admitted. Indeed, several monodic fragments having at least one of these features are known to be undecidable. We investigate these features systematically and show that fundamental monodic fragments such as the two-variable fragment with counting and the guarded fragment of standard first-order modal logics $\mathbf{K}_{n}$ and $\mathbf{S5}_{n}$ are decidable. Tight complexity bounds are established as well. Under the expanding-domain semantics, we show decidability of the basic modal logic extended with the transitive closure operator on frames without infinite ascending chains; this logic, however, is Ackermann-hard.

papers.title: Decomposable shuffles
papers.abstract: We develop a combinatorial and order-theoretic framework for shuffles, understood as ordered partitions of the natural numbers. We introduce decomposable shuffles as generalised sums of finite ordinals, copies of $\omega$, and copies of its dual $\omega^*$, indexed by countable scattered linear orders. These building blocks are called benches, ladders and snakes, respectively. We introduce a subclass, layered shuffles, and for this subclass we construct an explicit finite-address representation which reduces comparison in the induced order on $\mathbb N$ to lexicographic comparison of integer tuples. We determine the order types of represented layered shuffles, establish that all represented orders are scattered, and define an involution that realises order duality. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical composition on bench-free injective uniform shuffles of fixed sign. For each sign, this operation yields a monoid graded by reduced degree. Its degree-one component is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)$ and consists precisely of the invertible elements.

papers.title: Scott spectral gaps for trees are bounded
papers.abstract: Given a Borel class of trees, we show that there is a tree in that class whose Scott sentence is not too much more complicated than the definition of the class. In particular, if the class is definable by a $\Pi_\alpha$ sentence, then there is a model of Scott rank at most $\alpha + 2$. This gives another proof-and one that does not require first proving Vaught's conjecture for trees-of the fact that trees are not faithfully Borel complete.

papers.title: On Star operation and some ideals on the Baire space
papers.abstract: We investigate several $\sigma$-ideals on the Baire space $\omega^\omega$ $(\mathbb{Z}^\omega)$, introducing and studying the ideals $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{SMZ}^+$, alongside the classical ideals of meager sets, strong measure zero sets, the eventually different ideal and infinitely equal ideal We establish structural relationships and proper inclusions among these ideals. Also we compute the cardinal invariants of $\mathcal{M}_-$, proving that they are same as invariants of $\sigma$-ideal of meager sets. We further analyze the operation $^*$ on families of sets, establishing dual relationships such as $\mathcal{ED}^* = \mathcal{IE}$, $\mathcal{IE}^*=\mathcal{ED}$, $\mathcal{M}_-^*=\mathcal{SMZ}^+$ and $\mathcal{H}^* = \mathcal{G}$, and derive separations between ideals under additional set-theoretic assumptions. Finally, we prove a tree dichotomy theorem for the ideal $\mathcal{M}_-$ and we study the associated forcing notion.

papers.title: On Local Finiteness of Modal K4 Algebras
papers.abstract: We study local finiteness for modal $K4$ algebras via the tunability of their dual general frames. In particular, we provide a sufficient condition for modal $K4$ algebras to be locally finite by identifying a structure which must be present in non-locally finite modal $K4$ algebras. We then show that this condition becomes both necessary and sufficient for $\sigma$-complete modal $K4$ algebras. Next, we translate this condition into a pair of order-theoretic conditions on transitive Kripke frames, providing a classification of local finiteness on their dual modal algebras. We further show that the logic of any class of well-founded transitive relations with no infinite antichains has the finite model property, and conclude that the logic of the class of well-quasi orderings has the finite model property.
